transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we settle the authorization for the Line 4 closed-loop rinse-recovery skid, I need each technical specialist to enter their formal finding into the meeting record. As you know, the municipal water-conservation restriction begins Monday, and Line 4 currently uses fresh rinse water each shift. The skid is installed but hasn't been placed into production service yet. I'll need your findings on engineering readiness, compliance status, and any pending paperwork before I make the final utilities authorization and operating-control decision. Please go ahead.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Good morning, Mara. Here's my engineering finding for the record. My commissioning trial on the Line 4 closed-loop rinse-recovery skid found that loop conductivity reaches 1,200 microsiemens per centimeter after 40 cycles, while Line 4's rinse specification allows no more than 900. The validated operating plan is to purge exactly 300 liters every 30 cycles to stay within spec. The skid vendor confirmed that pump-seal replacement and recommissioning require exactly 6 hours. However, my trial worksheet is still awaiting engineering signoff, so that is pending paperwork. I'll formally reveal the specific details now.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Good morning, Mara. Here is my compliance finding for the record. My permit review, confirmed with the regulator yesterday, requires every recovery-loop purge to be neutralized to a pH from exactly 7.13 through 7.47, with a sample collected during the first 90 seconds of each purge before discharge and an entry made for every purge in the wastewater log. I have not yet attached the regulator's note to the utility change record, so that is pending compliance paperwork.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Engineering signoff on commissioning trial worksheet for the Line 4 closed-loop rinse-recovery skid must be completed before start.
Regulator's note must be attached to the utility change record before start.
